title: Do not recommend to buy from this seller
text:
I ordered this toy set for my nephew’s birthday and regretted it almost immediately. The product arrived late and the packaging was damaged — the box was crushed and taped up, which already set a bad first impression. When we opened it, several pieces were missing and a few parts were warped and didn’t fit together properly. The instructions were unclear and had typos, so assembling it turned into a frustrating guessing game.

The materials feel cheap and flimsy; thin plastic that creaks and bends too easily. Within a day of my nephew playing, a small connector snapped clean off during normal use. That made part of the set unusable, and he was disappointed. I tried contacting the seller for a replacement or refund, but received a delayed, generic response that didn’t address the missing parts or offer a clear solution. After more back-and-forth I was told to file a claim through Amazon — which is extra hassle for something that should have been complete and sturdy out of the box.

For the price, I expected better quality and service. This was a poor experience overall: damaged packaging, missing and broken pieces, shoddy instructions, and unhelpful seller communication. I do not recommend buying from this seller.

title: A Funny Man Revealed
text:
I remember watching Steve Martin's seemingly meteoric rise from Tonight Show guest, to Saturday Night Live stalwart, to concert hall blockbuster. He made me laugh. He helped take the edge off the 70's. I remember leaving one of his Nassau Coliseum shows thinking that all in the world was good and it's ok to be goofy - for a little while anyway. It was from that melancholy recollection I read through this book.

While Martin's stand up humor was edgy, innovative, and visual, Born Standing Up is laced with a dry humor that sometimes brings chuckles one or two lines afterward. We can see that as is true for most seemingly overnight success stories there are years of hard work and sacrifice behind the sensation. Though there is only a small window into Steve's creative genius, you can see how his young life contributed to the product he presented on stage. Martin's stand up act was filled with silliness, idiocy, and just plain tomfoolery. In Born Standing Up we see the crafting of that act took an intellectual approach and technical dissection of how comedy works. Laced with stories of his family life, upstart employment, inspirations, encounters and collaborations with familiar performers from the era, and the eventual eruption of his show, Born Standing Up leads down a road of opportunities realized and acted upon.

Tracking the career of Steve Martin can be confusing. The performances of the stand up era are dramatically different from the ones we see in movies today. So different that when I played some of "Let's Get Small" for my kids (who are very familiar with the Cheaper by the Dozen dad) they had a hard time believing it is the same person. Born Standing Up reveals an underlying personality that is constant throughout Martin's career.

I believe this is a 5 star book for anyone who fondly remembers Martin's stand-up. Thanks Steve for making the world a little less serious!

title: Excellent narrative but questionable claims
text:
This is an excellent narrative history of contributors, ideas, movements, and events in German culture. Peter Watson communicates his encyclopaedic knowledge very readably. He summarises major thinkers and cultural movements concisely, but rigorously, with a great gift for succinct meaningful précis.

However, Watson’s claim that the extent of the German contribution to modernity is unique (eg page 828 on ‘The First XI of Modern History’ which includes Mendel!), is unsustainable. Roy Porter claims otherwise in his ‘Enlightenment: Britain and the Creation of the Modern World’ as does Sudhir Hazareesingh in ‘How the French Think’. It is in any case a claim which lends support to the objectionable idea of German superiority. Renaissance and Enlightenment were pan-European projects.

Watson’s interesting thesis is that Pietism, Bildung and Innerlichkeit account for the German genius, but he does not show how these qualities of individual worth and spirituality fit with a strong tendency to communal obedience in German culture. He does however show how nationalism was initially a liberal idea challenging the old illiberal autocratic feudal German states.

Watson does not cover the major contribution of church, particularly in post-war German society. The West German Protestant church established the bi-annual ‘Kirchentag’ movement dedicated to persuade the German Christian to follow individual conscience rather than state dictat, and to include the outsider. The East German church hosted the political reform movement that led to ‘die Wende’, although the East’s DDR resisted acknowledgement of Holocaust guilt for too long.

Watson has provided a mine of data for a fuller debate on the causal factors, the nature, and the extent of the German contribution.

The key to getting the most out of it was learning the mouse feature; it’s a little quirky at first but once you get the hang of it, navigation becomes smooth and intuitive.

The mouse emulation takes a tiny learning curve. Initially I expected a standard pointer, but it behaves more like a touchpad cursor that you control with the remote. For web browsers and web-based apps I use often (including Hulu via browser access), the mouse feature is indispensable — it makes clicking through links, filling in login fields, and controlling playback far easier than relying on directional buttons alone.

Performance is solid. Streaming Hulu and other services runs reliably; video quality is consistent and I haven’t experienced significant buffering beyond what I expect from my home internet. XBMC/Kodi integration is excellent and allows me to organize my media the way I like. The unit is compact, quiet, and doesn’t heat up noticeably during long viewing sessions.

If you’re comfortable with a little initial tweaking and getting used to the mouse control, this product is a great value. It expanded my TV’s capabilities and made web browsing and streaming on the big screen practical. Highly recommend for anyone wanting an affordable way to run XBMC/Kodi and access web-based services like Hulu.

text: This cage is bigger than I thought, and is perfect for my indian ringneck parakeet! She loves it! I would not put a bird with feet smaller than an indian ringneck's in this cage,  as a smaller bird will not be able to climb the walls in this cage. King's cages are well-known for being top-of-the-line and well-built, and this cage lives up to that expectation.  I purchased the white version that has the 5/8" bar spacing (it is also available with 1" bar spacing), it arrived by frieght delivery in pieces in two boxes on a pallet and was very well-packed, so I was able to pre-schedule the delivery date. It came with vague assembly instructions, but was fairly easy to put together. I was able to assemble the entire cage by myself, which was an accomplishment for a 5-foot tall woman! The perches are HUGE (basically for a cockatoo or double-yellowhead amazon size bird), so I purchased 3/4" unsealed/untreated pine dowels at Home Depot, cut them to the lengths I needed and notched them. One engineering issue I found with this cage is that the placement of the door is too far to the right, which makes it impossible to run a perch all the way across the cage in front of the food and water dishes. King's could have avoided this problem by just shifting the door about 2-inches to the left. I solved this problem using PVC pipe and fittings from the plumbing section of a home improvement store. The locks on this cage are bird-proof.  I love this cage! It is beautiful, sturdy, very well-made, roomy, and has a built-in play stand. My bird loves it, too!

text: I purchased this set of adhesive hooks with high hopes for organizing my home office, specifically to hang my coffee mug organizer and some lightweight tools above my desk. The concept seemed perfect for avoiding holes in the wall and keeping my workspace clutter-free without needing to drill or use unsightly command strips that often leave marks. The packaging looked professional, and the instructions were clear, promising a bond that lasts for months rather than days. Unfortunately, the reality of using this product was a stark disappointment that I never expected given the positive reviews I had read prior to buying. On the first day of installation, I carefully cleaned the surface of the wall with the provided alcohol wipe, pressed the hook firmly for the recommended thirty seconds, and waited the full hour before hanging anything. I hung a small, lightweight basket filled with pens and paperclips. Within less than four hours, I heard a distinct thud from the corner of my eye. Rushing over, I found the basket on the floor, shards of plastic scattered everywhere, and the adhesive hook lying limp and useless against the baseboard. It had not just failed to hold the item; it had completely detached itself from the wall, leaving no residue but a significant mess. I tried again with a different hook and a slightly heavier bag of tissues. This time, it lasted only six hours before falling again. I understand that surfaces can vary, but claiming a strong bond for months is misleading when the product cannot even survive a standard workday. For the price, I expected basic reliability, not constant cleaning up of dropped items. The adhesive seems weak and inconsistent, with no guarantee that it will stick properly regardless of how well you follow the instructions. If you are looking for a temporary solution for something that absolutely must not fall, this might work for ten minutes, but for any practical, long-term office organization, it is a waste of money. Do not trust the initial stickiness; it is not reliable. I have since switched to traditional command strips, which are more expensive but actually stay on the wall as advertised. Save your time and frustration, and avoid this product entirely.

title: If the rest is like the first chapter....
text:
...run, not walk away.

I was pleased to see this on offer from Vine and as I'm currently considering a move to Win8, gladly picked this up. If Win8 itself is as unclear as this book, I'll be sticking to Win7.

The first chapter, page 20 "using the taskbar and start button". Huh? I thought the Start button was gone? The section then goes on to say how you can use the "pin to start" button to pin an app to the start menu. What? You mean the start screen? And where's the start button you promised to talk about? In less than four pages, the authors refer to the (I'm assuming) Start Screen as start button, menu and screen.

I decide to use the index which lists "Start Menu, classic" and points to pages 562-3. That describes a "hidden system menu".

I'm sure to get this out the door, they worked with beta and early release products, but even their editors couldn't get naming down? In the first chapter, they couldn't see the authors were referring to one thing using many terms? Worse, they were using terms from previous versions of Windows. Even worse, the specific term was one that's brought a lot of criticism to MS about Win8.

Wow.

title: Cheap.  Does what I need it to do.  Works with Windows 10.
text:
It's dirt cheap, it connects via bluetooth, and has a built-in trackpad. I use this little keyboard to control my Windows 10 Surface Pro 2 when I have it hooked to the TV for starting up gaming/video sessions (with an Xbox 360 controller taking the USB port) or if I have it hooked to a monitor at the office. While it's not as good a keyboard as the surface pro type cover or some of the fancier/pricier options from Logitech, I'm satisfied given the price.

The keyboard has a built-in battery and charges via USB - one microUSB cable is included if you don't already have one. So far, it seems to hold a charge for a while, as at this point I've only had to charge it once.

If you're packing the keyboard in a bag, make sure to pack it close to something that will give it support, as it's quite thin and would probably flex and get damaged if just carelessly tossed in a bag with a bunch of other stuff.

Some other reviewers said that the keyboard slides around if put on a desk. Mine came with stick-on rubber feet (included in the box) that solved the sliding problem.

Edit: One additional issue I noticed after using it for a while. It doesn't seem that you can disable the "tap to click" feature on the trackpad through Windows 10. This is probably due to the drivers Windows selects for the device, but it still may cause an issue for some potential purchasers who get annoyed with accidentally clicking stuff with their trackpads.

As for the sound, is it loud? Yea a bit, obviously it's louder than a normal keyboard, but I actually enjoy it, and joyfully clack the keys. It's really not that loud, maybe if you were in a empty room with high ceilings were it could echo would you find this a issue. I dont really see any gamer that is enough into gaming that they would A. want a mech keyboard, and B. pay this much for a keyboard having an issue with it. Just don't try using it in the same room your GF is sleeping...

Improvements/cons? Wish you could adjust the back light levels and color, and maybe 5 more macro buttons by the space bar would be lovely (i'm sick i know). The ONE con i do have, its that sometimes my space bar sticks, its VERY VERY rare- and i can't say that is actually a design flaw- it could be a cookie cumb or something... heh. So, i wouldnt suggest nibbling on something around it.
Great job Razer. Oh and btw, when i've had issues with past items (naga mouse addon being buggy), the razer tech guys were amazing and intense about figuring out my problem (Screen shots etc).

Carl believed that Elena was destined to be his wife and he was overcome with despair when she finally succumbed to her illness. He decided that even death could not keep them apart, and he exhumed his bride and brought her body back to his home, where he cleaned it up and used an elaborate embalming process to preserve her remains. He kept her there with him for 8 years, during which time she naturally began to fall apart a bit, but Carl kept her looking as good as possible by filling in her sunken features with wax. He even inserted a tube in her vaginal canal so they could consummate their love. Yes, it doesn't get much sicker than this! title: Erik Larson leaves us wanting more...
text:
I read Erik Larson's book with great curiosity and high expectations, given the stellar reviews it has received in the media and academia. After finishing it, I have to admit I was torn between contradictory feelings:
- on one hand, the research is exhaustive and the reconstruction of the time he covers (basically July 1933-June 1934) is awesome, with great character depiction and an amazing ability to make intrigues in the State Department and events in Berlin come alive.
- on the other hand, the book left me deeply frustrated for at least 2 major reasons:

1) some major questions are left completely unanswered, esp. was Martha Dodd a Soviet spy? How did her obvious promiscuity not constitute more of an issue for the State Department, her father or a vulnerability to the German secret services?

2) even more importantly, what happens after the Night of the Long Knives (June 30, 1934)??? Dodd stayed in post until December 1937, i.e. another three and a half years (!) but barely a word is said about events during that time and his role in the American reaction to these events.

I would understand this silence if nothing had happened between June 1934 and the Anschluss, but there were extraordinary events that deserved at least a mention:
- the assassination of the Austrian chancellor Engelbert Dollfuss, which led to major tension between Germany and Italy, and took place less than a month after the June 1934 "epilogue" to the book
- the Saar referendum in January 1935
- the introduction of the Nuremberg laws in September 1935
- the referendum and remilitarization of Rhineland in March 1936
- the start of the Spanish Civil war in July 1936
All of these events were major milestones in the accession of Hitler to absolute power and the unstoppable march towards a world war, and it is unthinkable that Dodd (or Larson for that matter) has nothing to say about them... If the sources or archival materials dried up after Dodd's first year in Germany, why doesn't Larson tell us so and explain why he covers only the first 22% or so of his tenure as US ambassador !!!

Overall, a great read, but one that barely scratches the surface of a fascinating subject.

title: The "gateway drone" for beginners
text:
I've never owned a drone before so didn't know what to expect. This package contains two zippable pouches with a folded controller and drone, which are both tiny. You have to charge both units before attempting anything, and the charging station isn't obvious to use. Next, install the app on your phone and it will sync with the drone later.

Once unfolded, there is a calibration process you must follow before flying, which is a minor inconvenience but you learn the routine pretty quickly. The controller has a number of directional buttons but the easiest way to learn is to go outside in a large, clear area and experiment - after about an hour of flight time, you can get very proficient with the joysticks.

The unit broadcasts video back to your phone (or records to the provided SD card) and it's entertaining to watch your flight experience. This is not a stabilized gimbal so don't expect SteadiCam-style gliding - it can get a little rough at times - and there's no audio.

The machine will hover by itself with very little drift, and the return to home button works well. There is an option to use indoors but it's not a great idea - I decapitated a houseplant, nipped on my fingers and almost destroyed a light fixture. Without the GPS (and in the hands of a novice), indoor flying isn't particularly safe.

This drone is a good unit for beginners, older kids and supervised children, and can get you used to the basics of how drone operation works. After a few flights, you'll find yourself wanting to upgrade to something more expensive with more features, but at this price level it's a great way to learn the ropes.

And like I said, blade out or not, it works great as a fist reinforcing kubotan, plus you can use the blunt end to gouge into someone's hand, face, etc. and get them to take a step back so you can make your getaway. title: Be careful what you ask for
text:
I got this book because I heard the author and her husband interviewed recently on NPR. Based on that, I thought "Wondering Who You Are" would be a uniquely uplifting story. I expected something along the lines of Jill Bolte Taylor's "My Stroke of Insight," which was a fascinating and inspiring first-hand account of a young woman's stroke and rehabilitation. For sure, this book did keep me on the edge of my seat - I couldn't put it down (as other reviewers have noted). And it did have some engaging parts, like the description of Richard's chaotic hospitalization, the couple's experience with a mediator over the legal settlement, and Lea's sexual exploration, among others. But I came away from the book feeling it was over-wrought and just plain sad. Here is a woman (the author) who actually leads a rich, surprising, adventure-filled life, but she just can't stop weeping over her lack of self-fulfillment. It's ironic that she spends so much of the book bemoaning the loss of her remarkable husband's pre-surgery personality, and yet while she had him that way, she was an alcoholic who preferred to be out partying rather than staying home with him and her children! Clearly she is transformed by her experience with him after he loses his personality, but she seems to find barely an ounce of delight in any of his rehabilitation successes or her own exploration of the wondrous possibilities life has to offer. Instead we hear too many times about her tears.

If nothing else, what this book teaches is - be careful what you ask for. If you long for unconditional love and acceptance, here is post-surgery Richard, able to offer these things in spades…. but it's creepy. Gurus like Byron Katie teach us the joy of living in the moment and questioning our personal narratives, but those approaches to self-transformation are only viable if we have a memory and a life story - as Richard does not.

title: Waaay better than the Swann I replaced
text:
[[VIDEOID:7ae84ae66b1c39445d7e5289bdae27ae]] I live in a 2nd story apartment and installed a Swann 2.4GHz wireless that I picked up from the local hardware store about a year ago. I installed it after scaring off some would-be car thief's. I decided to replace it because one of my receivers went out and I replaced it with the standard Astak 2.4GHz wireless receiver. I was impressed with the receiver (w/remote) and so I thought I'd give these cameras a try (the Swann was very choppy and I had to mess with the brightness controls in the software I use, a lot). I use the second receiver to hook to the TV in my living room. The cameras and receiver are in the same location as when I was using the Swann.

These cameras are way better than the Swann. The video that comes with this review was taken from my PC (I wire it through a Roxio RCA to USB connector) and use a freeware program to capture it (Debut). There are three walls between my computer and the cameras.

Others post about bad reception because of wireless routers. I don't use one, but there are several that appear in my wireless network list on my Windows PC. To be fair, they could have changed their routers after I installed the Swann a year ago.

Downside: The audio is choppy and has static. I don't use the audio; I didn't use the audio with the Swann, either. This is the reason for my "low" marks. Also, in the manual I discovered that in low light the cameras will switch to black and white. However, as you can see from the video, the b/w hasn't switched on. There is a big flood light in my parking lot which may be the reason. Color 24/7. Judge for yourself.

Tip: you may need to adjust the antenna on the receiver to get the lowest amount of static. I've found that moving it about 20 degrees at a time lets you see the difference.

Well worth the money. I hope this helps.

title: OK
text:
I bought this OK fitness tracker a few weeks ago after reading some mixed reviews and wanting something affordable to monitor steps and sleep. Overall I’m moderately satisfied — it does many things adequately but nothing outstanding.

Setup was straightforward and the companion app is simple to navigate, though a bit slow to sync at times. Step counting seems reasonably accurate for daily walks, but it occasionally misses short indoor steps or counts arm movements as steps when I’m doing dishes. Heart rate monitoring works well during steady-state cardio but lags during interval workouts and sometimes shows spikes that don’t match how I feel.

Battery life met the advertised claim; I got about five days between charges with regular use and notifications enabled. The band is comfortable enough for everyday wear and the display is readable in daylight, though a bit dim indoors at the lowest setting.

I appreciate the sleep-tracking feature, but the sleep stages feel approximate and sometimes label restless nights inaccurately. Customer support responded politely when I had a sync issue, but resolution took a few days.

If you want a budget-friendly tracker with basic features, this is fine. If you need highly accurate metrics for serious training, consider a step up.

text:

There are these little metal teeth on one side of the v-shaped recess. You just slide the jar into the recess as far as it will go and turn. The metal teeth grip the lid, so when you turn, you're actually unscrewing the jar from the lid instead of the lid from the jar. And it's really easy. Admittedly, I don't have arthritis in my hands, so I can't say how easy it would be with arthritis. But I am a single woman with limited arm and grip strength. Jars can be a challenge. Opening them with this is safer than banging on the edge of the lid with the handle of a butter knife. And easier, too.

I'd give it 5 stars, but I can't help but wonder about the longevity of the adhesive. Maybe if it's hanging upside down under my cabinet a year from now I'll come back and give it the 5th star. And yes, I did get this item at a reduce price in order to review it, but that does not effect my review. If you don't have integrity, what have you got?

There is no way to fix the flimsiness either. The spring is way too weak to hold it in place. Despite aggressive tightening of the single screw that holds each basket in place, the baskets still spin. Even the poles themselves are weak - just tapping the pole gently with my index finger makes the whole thing shake in a very threatening manner.

I needed two - one new, and one to replace my cheap, $16 plastic tension caddy. That tension caddy has been in place for over 9 years and is looking grungy now, but it has never budged from place and has solidly held anything I have placed upon it. It doesn't look as nice as a bronze caddy but at least it's functional.

It boggles my mind that somewhere in some office is the person responsible for bringing this piece of crap to market, and that person probably makes more money than you and I combined. That just adds insult to the injury of the $80 I wasted buying these things.

So, the second one I'm not even bothering to put together. I guess that I will give it as a gift at Christmas to someone I do not like.

He was found a stray dog running around the country in the winter. He's got some quirks but this barking is/was the worst. He's been an incredible hunter in our fenced backyard. Even as I write this, two German Shepard's and now some more dogs just came walking past our from window being walked around the neighborhood and all I heard from Rocky today is a light whimper. Rocky used to go ape-crazy, barking incessantly at every dog that strolls by, runner, deliver person, and mail person, anything would set him off barking like crazy. Church's perspective has become more important than ever.  Most of Newman's closest Oxford friends (I've counted about eleven of them), including Church, did not convert to the Roman Church.  Why?  Newman had such power and influence!  Yet Dean Church did not believe it was necessary to cross the Tiber in order to be a Catholic Christian. title: This book will change your life
text:
Whether you define success as achieving greater wealth, losing weight, or just being happy, this is one of the most invaluable books you will ever read. I especially appreciate the fact that the author is unequivocal about finding our passion and living a life of purpose -- becoming an active participant in the world rather than being a passive observer.

Perhaps the greatest difference between Mr. Alabi and me is that he leads a God-driven life and I am an atheist. Nonetheless, we share a very core outlook and understanding about becoming self-actualized people. And I don't remember highlighting a book so much along the way because there is real wisdom captured on almost every page. Having read many books about achieving success, I wasn't sure this book could offer much more. But it did. The amount of research and context with which this guide was written sets it far apart from all the rest. Read it for the case study of Abraham Lincoln alone -- I was stunned to learn of his immense struggles before achieving the greatness that is familiar to us all.

Lastly, for anyone who may be struggling, you need to run to buy this book today. It will put in perspective how everything in life is about attitude and approach and that what we may view as "failure" at one point, is simply a necessary step to taking us to where we need to be. Color coding makes things easier to identify, always, as opposed to seeing those bland green or manila folders in the drawer and you've got to thumb through them for awhile before you find the folder you're looking for. And there's so much room in these folders to condense your bills, papers, and things, that with my cell phone bills, I can nearly hold up to 4 years worth, and counting, within one folder!!! The folders are pretty sturdy with their metal sliding holders and can withstand the weight and/or the wear-n-tear of you pulling them out of the drawer and filling them every month or so. Also, the accordian-like stretchiness on the sides make them easy to condense or fill. My folders have been holding up for at least 2 years now and I'm sure they'll last me a life-time. I prefer getting these and filling up my metal filing cabinets with them as opposed to getting those plastic, flimsy filers that stand alone or come in plastic totes. Those could never accomodate all the filing I need to get done!!! Yes, so if you want to file and even be a little fashionable while doing it...buy these!!! Happy organizing!!!

In today's work ecosystem of forced multitasking, being "busy" all the time, and never feeling comfortable saying "no", Essentialism provides unique principles for sorting through the noise and figuring out what is truly "essential". The author himself says brilliantly that "essentialism is not one more thing -- it's a whole new way of doing everything". The key principles that I have uncovered from this book are the following:
(1) Work effectively, not efficiently (the latter does not imply that you are working on THE most important things)
(2) Learn to say no to things (personal, work, etc) and take greater control of your life
(3) Actively funnel to-do's, requests, etc through an internal "essential" test to decide whether something is truely important and should be done at all

One caveat, similar to many books in this genre. If you are a low-ranking associate at your job, you will find it difficult to implement a fair number of these strategies Day 1 (e.g. "how the hell am I supposed to do this while working at a [law firm / bank / advertising agency / etc]). That being said, the principles are still worth reading and keeping with you, because as you grow more senior in your role (even if you're just managing one person initially), they will become incrementally more valuable

title: Great Little Toy for Older Children and Adults
text:
I have been a fan of toy steam engines since I received a German made WILESCO engine for Christmas in 1961! This little engine by SunnyTech, a Chinese company, is very well made, with all brass parts, except for an O-ring to seal the boiler. When I first fired the engine up it ran like who-shot-john! I was rather amazed. This will make a great gift for any budding engineers that you may know, or any professional engineers, for that matter.
There are some pitfalls that the buyer should be aware of:
There are no instructions, at least in the one I bought has no instructions, just an exploded drawing showing how it should be put together. It is a good thing that I had experience with toy steam engines.
NEVER fill the boiler more than 2/3 full.
When running, it will spray some water, this is normal for a steam engine.
It does vibrate when running, place it on a stable surface.
The engine gets HOT when running. Take appropriate precautions.
Use alcohol as a fuel. Ethel or methyl alcohol (+95%) will work best. I tried 91% Isopropyl alcohol and it works fine, although it covered the boiler with soot. So you might want to avoid that.
NEVER use any petroleum derived fuel such as gasoline or Coleman fuel.
The engine is designed to only run for a few minutes on one boiler of water. Blow the lamp out immediately when the boiler is low on water or you may damage the engine with excess heat.
Remember, this is a toy but only for older children and adults.

title: Weak sequel compared to strong beginning
text:
When I first began this series, I was afraid I would not enjoy going back into Tortall's history, without any of the characters that have been the anchor of the Tortall series. It didn't help that the format was in first person, diary form. However, I was pleasantly surprised to find myself enjoying the books, and the story that revolves around Beka Cooper, George Cooper's ancestor, and guardswoman for the Provost's Guards. It gives a clear picture of the difficulties of the lives of people with no advantages and very little opportunity.

In Bloodhound, Beka is in Port Caynn, searching for the origin of the counterfeited coins that have been popping up in Corus. While the story is enjoyable, the length is not. By page 400, I was wishing that I was at the last page. The end seems to drag on without any resolution. It doesn't help that 'Beka' keeps writing in her diary that she is tired and must stop writing. I would think at her age and maturity, she wouldn't feel the need to write in her diary as if she were talking to it.
The final aspect that was irritating was the very casual, nonchalant way Pounce was disposed of from the list of characters. It was very poorly done, and he was inserted back into the story just as poorly.

As a final thought, would Beka laugh at the irony of knowing that her descendants would have the blood of Trebond as well?

Customer photos looked like the same issue others reported, so I wish I’d paid more attention to the reviews.

I contacted customer support and they were polite, but the replacement options felt like a band-aid rather than a fix; I didn’t want to keep exchanging several low-cost items hoping one would be okay. I am VERY happy with the unit. Packing was great; undamaged in transit. Instructions are clear enough, albeit not super. Menu system is also easy enough to use, but the 2-line LCD screen reminds me of my first fax machine 10 years ago. (The Dell had a full 5 line color screen.)

This Canon looks SLICK; very stylish. The front door automatically opens when it starts printing -- like a kid I will never get over how cool that is. It's very quick and the fax and copy functions work with one button.

It's pretty quiet (there's an option for Nighttime printing which I guess makes it even quieter) but shakes the desk when it's moving! Paper cassette holds plenty of paper and the auto feed handler works great for the fax.

The unit is BIG, though. Maybe not bigger than others, but much bigger than my old printer. If you're a work-at-home guy like me, you should measure your area before bying any of these units.

Right away I noticed that it gives a very natural-looking finish — when I use it during practice sessions it blends well and doesn’t look heavy or cakey under different lighting.

Application is easy; the formula is forgiving, so even on days when I’m rushing practice, it doesn’t smear or streak easily. It holds up reasonably well through a couple hours of rehearsal, sweat, and movement, though I do touch up before any longer sessions or performances. The scent is mild and not overpowering, which I appreciate.

What keeps this from being a full five stars is longevity and pigment intensity. For everyday practice it’s great, but if I’m doing a full show or a day with extended wear I need to reapply halfway through to maintain the same level of coverage. Also, if you prefer bold, dramatic looks, you might find the pigment a bit muted compared with other products I’ve tried; it’s tailored more to a natural finish.

A nice bonus is that it’s gentle on my skin—no irritation even after repeated use. Overall, a solid, reliable product for practice and casual wear that looks good and performs well enough. I’ll keep using it and would recommend it to others looking for a natural, easy-to-use option.

title: Much ado about--what?
text: Even when the plot or the theme doesn't do it for me, Dean Koontz's descriptive skill and unique turn of phrase can usually give me some enjoyment of his books. This time, it wasn't enough. Plenty of description, but  all too dark. Too many characters with too many sub-plots, too much jumping from scene to scene, too many chapters,  too many slimy monsters, too gruesome, too disgusting... It was as if the author had 55 ideas for horror stories, couldn't settle on which one to write, and tried to pack them all into one book. There even seemed to be a veiled attempt at "equal opportunity"--old folks, youngsters, Whites, Oriental, Asian, disabilities... I kept reading, thinking somewhere, somehow there would be a point to all the madness. if one existed, it eluded me completely, and at the end I just wondered why I had bothered. I'll stick with the Odd Thomas books. They at least have some fey humor to lighten the mood.
